correctness.rationale: The corrected RESULT.md proves the same exact aligned-area formula without assuming the frozen proof's false vertical extent [-h/2,h]. For a rectangle of horizontal half-side u and horizontal center s, its largest absolute abscissa is U=u+|s|. All vertical coordinates must lie in the intersection of the two exact disk intervals, whose lower endpoint is h-Q(U) because Q-P increases to 3h/2, and whose upper endpoint is -h/2+P(U). These bounds are sufficient as well as necessary. The true vertical extent is [h-1,h]. Area is bounded by 2u f(U) <= 2U f(U), with equality only at s=0 and full available height. Strict concavity gives the unique interior root; a rational bracket establishes noncentrality and unequal sides. The frozen u,v,c decimals were wrong at the stated precision; the repair gives the reproduced values without changing the exact result or the stated area. The bounded 80-digit Decimal replay used 120 bisection steps and found area 0.4197167574230241 and the four predicted contacts, with the other eight squared-distance slacks positive. No unrestricted-orientation claim is proved.
residual_risks: The numerical replay corroborates decimals and contacts, not the exact optimization proof.
